messages:
Sam: Noticing weird traffic distribution for the payment-checkout route. We rolled 5% canary but telemetry shows ~18% hits on canary nodes since ~08:15 UTC.
Anya: Who pushed the latest guard rules? Any header-based rules landed recently?
Jesse: I changed a header guard for internal QA yesterday: header x-internal-test -> route to canary. Shouldn't affect public traffic but maybe header leaking?
Marta: Telemetry trace shows a surge of requests with x-internal-test present coming from our edge healthcheck pool. 🤔
Lia: Edge healthcheck uses a probe that includes x-rt-meta and we recently unified header sets. Maybe the probe now accidentally sets x-internal-test. I flagged a PR that renamed test headers.
Sam: If the edge probe is setting that header, sticky session cookie on clients won't matter because header routing has higher precedence right? Our runtime doc says order: guard headers -> cookie affinity -> hash.
Jesse: Right. Runtime currently short-circuits if any guard header matches. I can push a change to lower precedence, but need to confirm console expectations.
Anya: UI rollout config says "guards run after affinity" in the UX text. That's a mismatch with runtime. oof.
Marta: Also noticed split telemetry tags use "split:canary_v2" but routing logs use "variant:canary-2026-03" — mismatch prevents accurate accounting for console. We should unify tag names.
deploy-bot: config-change:payment-checkout at 2026-03-14T08:09:52Z by Jesse (guard: x-internal-test -> canary)
Lia: Proposal: emergency patch at edge to strip x-internal-test from healthcheck pool, short-term fix. Then follow-up: runtime precedence audit + console copy fix.
Sam: Agreed. Also we need an invariant test in rollout e2e: synthetic traffic that simulates cookie sticky + header present should follow documented precedence.
Jesse: I can revert the guard in config and open an RFC for precedence semantics. Will also add telemetry mapping to the rollout service.
Marta: I'll update the dashboard to show both routing tags side-by-side so we can detect mismatches quickly.
Anya: Who's owning the postmortem/QA checklist? We should include steps: strip header at edge, revert guard, add unit tests, fix console wording, and harmonize tags.
Sam: Assigning owners: Lia -> strip header; Jesse -> revert guard + RFC; Marta -> dashboard; Anya -> doc/QA checklist. I'll monitor and post status.
Lia: On it. Patching edge now, ETA ~10m.
Jesse: Reverting guard in 2m.
Marta: Dashboard draft link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/checkout-routing (wip)
Anya: Adding checklist to the incident doc.
Sam: Thanks team. Follow-up: add a small simulation harness to the rollout service that emits both "split" and "variant" tags for a subset of traffic so we can validate mappings automatically.
